install_notes: py -3.12 -m venv .venv; pip install pystac-client planetary-computer stackstac numpy dask rasterio psutil truststore: all binary wheels on py3.12 Windows 11, no build issues. On this machine Norton Antivirus intercepts TLS, so (a) truststore is needed for STAC/sign requests and (b) GDAL/libcurl (schannel) needs GDAL_CURL_CA_BUNDLE pointing at a PEM exported from the Windows ROOT store; plain CURL_CA_BUNDLE did NOT work. TLS verification stays on.
problems: Missed the 60 s bar: best cold run 69.0 s (search 5.0 s + load 64.0 s); other runs 88-111 s. Load is dominated by ~3,800 small remote COG window reads (546 items x 7 bands) and varies a lot run to run.
stackstac 0.5.1 + numpy 2 rejects fill_value=0 for dtype uint16; workaround fill_value=np.uint16(0).
Local TLS interception (Norton) breaks certifi and GDAL's schannel default; fixed with truststore + GDAL_CURL_CA_BUNDLE (see install_notes). Other Windows machines without Norton may not need this.
Single 1984-2026 search returns all months (1420 items) and took 26.8 s; parallel per-year Jun-Sep searches cut it to ~5-7 s.
More threads (128) and GDAL HTTP/2 multiplex tuning did not help; results were within network noise or worse.
notes: Best run: per-year parallel STAC search (16 threads), dask threaded scheduler with 64 workers, chunksize=1024 (one chunk per item-band), bounds_latlon AOI, epsg=32611, resolution=30, dtype=uint16, fill_value=0, rescale=False. 546 Jun-Sep scenes with cloud<50 from Landsat 4/5/7/8/9; red nonzero pixel fraction 0.868 (fill/edge pixels = 0). Per-year median red reflectance (all valid pixels, no cloud masking) is in median_red_reflectance_by_year and rises from ~0.04-0.07 in 1984-85 to ~0.18-0.21 after 2005, consistent with Lake Mead's falling water exposing bright shoreline. Idea to get under 60 s not tested here: load fewer scenes (e.g. best 3-5 per year by cloud cover, ~150-200 items) since per-scene read latency dominates.
